newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich debuts in style on London exchange.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich debuts in style on London exchange.

text.p: Woolwich Plc, the mortgage lender that has turned itself into a bank, stormed onto the stock market Monday, giving shareholders larger-than-anticipated windfalls fuelled by takeover speculation.

Woolwich shares made their debut at 368 pence ($6.23), offering a potential average windfall of 2,418 pounds ($4,091) to its depositors and borrowers, but the stock slipped back to 338.5 pence ($5.73) in the afternoon.

Chief Executive John Stewart told Reuters a combination of a buoyant market, a strong banking sector and the fact Woolwich was "a very attractive set of businesses" were behind what he admitted was a higher-than-expected price.
Dealers said the price squeeze was the combination of takeover talk in the market and a lack of available stock, but predicted the shares would lose ground.
Woolwich shed a 150-year tradition as a mutual company to convert to a bank and issue shares on the stock exchange.
With issued capital of around 1.6 billion shares, Woolwich will have a market capitalisation of about 5.5 billion pounds ($9.3 billion) at the share prices seen on its first day.
This would make it one of Britain's top-10 banks and one of the largest public companies when it joins the FTSE-100 index in September.
